data.narrative:
Quaise Energy is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde. The target operates within a sector represented by 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. The company has raised $134M to date.

The valuation analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, which is the sole applicable triangulation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($134M) as a base-value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, the analysis implies a post-raise valuation of $268M. This reflects the expected value expansion between Series A and subsequent funding stages. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparable data points within the Climate & Energy sector—while 8 same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow stage and valuation-tier filters yielded three or more datapoints necessary for robust median estimation.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $228M (low) to $308M (high), with a central estimate of $268M. The range reflects sensitivity around the stage-progression step-up multiple. Key uncertainties include the absence of tightly comparable peer financials at the same stage and the reliance on a single methodological approach. Subsequent rounds incorporating market data from active Series B fundraising or updated peer exits would strengthen conviction in this range.
